chapterNote: The first of the five Hallelujah psalms that close the Psalter — each begins and ends with 'Praise the LORD' — and the one that teaches, before the celebration gets loud, where not to put your weight. Do not trust nobles, sons of dust with no saving power in them: their breath goes out, they return to the ground, and their plans die the same day. Against that obituary the psalm sets the beatitude of the one whose help is the God of Jacob — and then it says why He can be trusted: He made heaven, earth, and sea; He keeps faith forever; and His record is the list of people the powerful step over. Justice for the oppressed, bread for the hungry, prisoners freed, blind eyes opened, the bent straightened, the righteous loved, the sojourner, orphan, and widow guarded — while the wicked's road is twisted into nothing. Isaiah 61 takes this list up, and when Jesus read Isaiah in Nazareth He claimed it as His own commission. The last line answers the third: princes die; the LORD reigns forever, your God, O Zion, through every generation.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Let my very soul praise the LORD!
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD ['Hallelujah', halelu-Yah, the KJV margin]. Praise [halal] the LORD [YHWH], O my soul [nephesh].
1.notes: The closing Hallelujah quintet (146-150) begins: each of the last five psalms opens and shuts with halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050). Before the congregation, the cosmos, or the orchestra is summoned, the singer starts with his own nephesh (H5315) — praise begins in the first person.

2.text: I will praise the LORD as long as I live; I will make music to my God while I still have being.
2.amp: While I live [chay] will I praise [halal] the LORD [YHWH]: I will sing praises [zamar] unto my God [Elohim] while I have any being.
2.notes: be-chayyai (H2416) and be-odi: as long as I live, as long as I am — praise made coterminous with existence. zamar (H2167) leans instrumental — make music, often to strings — so the resolution is to keep the music going to the last breath.

3.text: Do not put your trust in nobles, in a son of man, who has no power to save.
3.amp: Put not your trust [batach] in princes [nadib — nobles], nor in the son [ben] of man [adam], in whom there is no help ['salvation', teshuah, the KJV margin].
3.notes: The first thing praise teaches is where NOT to lean: nedibim (H5081), the powerful, are ben adam (H1121, H120) — sons of Adam, ground-born men (cf. verse 4) — with no teshuah (H8668), no saving power, in them. Psalm 118:9's rule restated for the last page; batach (H982) belongs elsewhere.

4.text: His breath goes out, he returns to his earth; on that very day his plans perish.
4.amp: His breath [ruach] goes forth [yatsa], he returns [shub] to his earth [adamah — his ground]; in that very day [yom] his thoughts [eshtonah — plans, schemes] perish [abad].
4.notes: The prince's obituary in one line: ruach yatsa, shub la-adamah (H7307, H3318, H7725, H127) — the breath leaves, the man goes back to the adamah he was named for — and his eshtonot (H6250), his policies and promises, abad (H6) the same afternoon. Every trust placed in him dies with him.

5.text: Oh the blessedness of the one whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope rests on the LORD his God —
5.amp: Happy [esher] is he that has the God [El] of Jacob [Yaaqob] for his help [ezer], whose hope [seber] is in the LORD [YHWH] his God [Elohim]:
5.notes: The Psalter's last beatitude: ashre (H835). El Yaaqob (H410, H3290) — the God of the schemer who was made a prince — as ezer (H5828), the helper-word of Eden's 'help meet' (Genesis 2:18). seber (H7664) is expectation resting its full weight; contrast the prince who could bear none.

6.text: the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them, who keeps faith forever;
6.amp: Which made [asah] heaven [shamayim], and earth [eretz], the sea [yam], and all that therein is: which keeps [shamar] truth [emeth] for ever [olam]:
6.notes: Why this Helper does not fail like the prince: He asah (H6213) the whole inventory — shamayim, eretz, yam (H8064, H776, H3220) — and He shamar emeth le-olam (H8104, H571, H5769), keeps faith forever. Creator-power and covenant-reliability, the two things a son of man cannot offer.

7.text: who does justice for the oppressed, who gives bread to the hungry. The LORD sets prisoners free;
7.amp: Which executes [asah] judgment [mishpat] for the oppressed [ashaq — the exploited]: which gives [natan] food [lechem] to the hungry [raeb]. The LORD [YHWH] looses [natar] the prisoners [asar — the bound]:
7.notes: The catalogue Isaiah 61:1 takes up and Jesus claimed as fulfilled when He read it in Nazareth's synagogue (cf. Luke 4:18-21): mishpat for the ashuqim (H4941, H6231), lechem for the reevim (H3899, H7457), the asurim (H631) loosed — the same word Isaiah uses for 'them that are bound'. In the Psalter God's praise is grounded in what He does for the people nobles overlook.

8.text: the LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD lifts up those who are bent low; the LORD loves the righteous;
8.amp: The LORD [YHWH] opens [paqach] the eyes of the blind [ivver]: the LORD raises [zaqaph — straightens up] them that are bowed down [kaphaph]: the LORD loves [ahab] the righteous [tsaddiq]:
8.notes: Five sentences in verses 7-9 begin 'YHWH' — the Name as anaphora. paqach ivrim (H6491, H5787), opening blind eyes, is in the Old Testament an act only God performs — which is why Jesus doing it was a claim (cf. John 9:32). zaqaph kephuphim (H2210, H3721): straightening the bent, the woman of Luke 13:11-13; and ahab tsaddiqim (H157, H6662), the loved righteous.

9.text: the LORD watches over the sojourners; He sustains the orphan and the widow — but the way of the wicked He bends crooked.
9.amp: The LORD [YHWH] preserves [shamar] the strangers [ger — resident aliens]; He relieves [ud — upholds, restores] the fatherless [yatom] and widow [almanah]: but the way [derek] of the wicked [rasha] He turns upside down [avat — bends crooked].
9.notes: The Torah's protected triad — ger, yatom, almanah (H1616, H3490, H490) — shamar'd and ud'd (H8104, H5749) by God personally. And the one negative in the catalogue: the rasha's derek (H7563, H1870) avat (H5791), bent until it goes nowhere. The same hand that straightens the bowed bends the crooked.

10.text: The LORD will reign forever — your God, O Zion, through all generations. Praise the LORD!
10.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall reign [malak] for ever [olam], even your God [Elohim], O Zion [Tsiyyon], unto all generations [dor va-dor]. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
10.notes: The answer to verse 3's princes: yimlokh YHWH le-olam (H4427, H5769) — one King whose breath does not go out and whose plans do not perish. Elohayikh Tsiyyon (H430, H6726), YOUR God, Zion: the eternal reign made personal, le-dor va-dor (H1755). halelu-Yah closes the frame.
